analysis.is_complaint_reason: Customer expresses dissatisfaction that their debit card was wrongly blocked by the bank's fraud system, causing them to be unable to pay a hotel and incur £47 roaming charges, and requests a refund. This alleges financial loss and material inconvenience under CH-1.
analysis.summary: Customer's debit card was blocked on 18/10/2026 by the bank's fraud system while they were on holiday in Spain. They could not pay their hotel and spent about two hours on the phone to have the block lifted, which they say cost £47 in roaming charges. They are asking for the £47 to be refunded. The complaints handler's note says the block was lifted after ID&V and the call lasted 1h52m per records. No vulnerability was noted. The customer prefers contact by email. The case file contains only the fraud block record and the call log, so the cause of the block and the link between the call and the roaming charges are not yet verified.

timeline.event: Debit card blocked by fraud system while customer was on holiday in Spain; customer unable to pay hotel
Fraud block lifted after ID&V; call duration 1h52m per records

analysis.severity_reason: Claimed financial loss is £47, which is under £100 (CH-6 Low). The customer also describes inconvenience while abroad, but the case does not show distress. Severity is set at Low on the stated loss; this would rise if the loss is confirmed to be higher or if the fraud block is shown to be a repeated issue.

vulnerability.suggested_support: None indicated in the case. The handler's note records no vulnerability, but the case does not say the customer was asked about support needs. Confirm no support needs during contact.

analysis.routing_reason: No ESC-1 trigger is met. The case does not involve suspected fraud against the customer, unauthorised transaction, lending, vulnerability referral, systemic issue, legal threat, media contact or a systems failure needing technical investigation on the case as written. The block was a fraud-system action, so the handler should check whether the fraud system needs technical investigation before deciding; if it does, Digital Operations would be the team (ESC-1). Handler to confirm.
